question: How can the sensation of touch occur if an external object is impossible?
premises: An external object may be impossible or absent.
The excellent touch is reflected within one's own self.
This internally reflected touch operates within some continuum of channels.
inference: Even without an external object, the internally reflected touch produces a pleasurable sensation within the body's channels.
uncertainties: The precise physiological or subtle-body meaning of nāḍisaṃtatau (continuum of channels) depends on broader Tantric context.
plain_english: When an external object is impossible, that same excellent touch, reflected within one's own self, produces that pleasurable sensation. It does so within some continuum of subtle channels.
